goal.encoding: medium/fast; zstd level 9 used for the joint prototype

joint_models: Message numeric lanes are specific to templates, with literal spelling and decimal/hex width preserved.
Parameters can be stably grouped by source node; the decoder derives the permutation from the header and template selector.
A parameter can store a residual of an earlier parameter or of its last value on the same source node.
Ordered microsecond clock gaps use 10 literal low bits, adaptive arithmetic coding of the high part conditioned on the previous gap and source equality, and a sparse overflow stream.
Epoch seconds and dotted dates are reconstructed from the clock; timezone offsets and the presence of an empty message separator are stored explicitly.

memory_error_parameters.scope: numeric lane buffers, zstd 9; excludes template/header costs

kernel_exception_parameters.scope: numeric lane buffers, zstd 9; excludes template/header costs

factored_nodes.result: rejected: about six additional seconds for 0.2 percent overall

core_id_to_node_affine_bits.result: about 85 KB, insufficient for the target; not integrated

periodic_clock_predictors.result: all larger than first-order clock gaps in the byte-plane probe

low_clock_bits.qualification: marginal entropy is not an information-theoretic lower bound; it does not rule out conditional predictors

limitations: The .bgj wrapper is an experimental reference codec, not a supported zform format.
It buffers the full corpus, shares message models across the entire file, and has no message query index; the header subarchive retains its standard index.
Whole-file grouping changes random-access costs and memory use. These results do not establish the same gain for independently decodable 32 MiB blocks.
Timings are single runs including preprocessing and file I/O, excluding compilation. Baseline timing is the earlier measurement, not an interleaved speed benchmark.
